scope: phase-aware channel copresence for a same-boot distance-one AirDrop target

research.finding: Unicast eligibility must phase-correct and intersect the synchronization schedule with the selected target's own advertised channel sequence. Following only the elected synchronization parent's schedule is insufficient as a general unicast gate.

hardwareExperiments.name: phase-aware-airdrop-target
hardwareExperiments.qualification: The capture exposed repeated use of one overlap interval. The implementation was subsequently corrected and host-regressed to select only a future guarded interval.

result.confirmed: The ESP can derive and execute guarded channel-6 intervals in which both its current synchronization schedule and the selected distance-one AirDrop target's advertised schedule report channel 6. Every transmitted MIF, Neighbor Solicitation, and Echo Request completed successfully at the radio. A post-correction control remained passive when no AirDrop target was present.
result.notConfirmed: The selected distance-one peer returned no directed response, so target copresence was not sufficient for admission. The one-burst-per-window correction has host coverage but did not encounter an AirDrop target in its post-correction hardware control.
result.nextFocus: Compare espDrop's minimal transmitted MIF and peer-admission state with current Apple MIFs while preserving the phase-aware target gate.
